name: Inked Crosshatch Storybook
description: A dark scene look — thick-line pen and ink with dense cross-hatching, the way an engraved graphic novel prints, held to dark teal and amber and lit by low warm light. Built to survive on a cheaper image model, because line art either lands or does not.
style_bible: Thick-line pen and ink illustration printed the way an engraved graphic novel prints. Medium and surface: every form is drawn first in confident black line of uneven weight — heavy on the contour and on the shadow side, thinning to a hairline where a surface turns into the light — and every value inside those contours is built from hatching rather than from paint: single hatch for a half tone, cross-hatch for a deep one, and a third crossing layer only in the darkest recesses, with the strokes following the form the way an engraver's burin would rather than lying flat. Stipple is permitted for grain, plaster and old paper; a smooth airbrushed gradient is not, anywhere, at any size. Colour is laid under the ink as flat, slightly uneven washes with visible edges, never as rendering: the whole image is held to dark teal and slate blue for everything the light has not reached and warm amber and ochre for everything it has, with the paper's own bone-white left bare for the brightest accents and no third hue given any real area. Subject grammar: one clear focal subject, with any further figure small, incidental and turned away or seen at a distance; the setting is built in layered depth around it. Lighting: one dominant low-key light direction, placed so the hatching can radiate from it, with the pool of light drawn as bare paper and thinning hatch, the mid-ground crossed once, and the corners crossed twice and going to solid black. No second source, no ambient lift, no glow bloom. Framing: sixteen by nine, a deliberate one-point or two-point perspective with a clear near edge so the eye enters at the bottom of the frame and travels to the lit thing; one third of the frame left as quiet dark. Robustness: the look is deliberately line-first so that it survives a cheaper or lower-fidelity image model — the drawing carries it, and no part of the contract depends on subtle rendering, correct skin, or fine facial detail. Keep the contract content-independent: no fixed individual, era, institution, room, event or copied composition.
negative_prompt: photoreal, photograph, photorealistic camera render, film still, 3D render, octane render, ray tracing, soft airbrush, smooth gradient, digital gloss, glossy highlights, blurred edges, soft focus, bokeh, depth of field blur, glow bloom, lens flare, saturated colour, candy colour, neon, magenta and cyan, rainbow palette, pastel palette, flat vector with no line weight variation, cel shading, anime, manga, chibi, cartoon proportions, watercolour bleed, oil impasto, readable lettering, captions, signatures, watermarks, frames, borders, UI elements, large face close to camera, head-and-shoulders crop, crowd, tissue or wound texture, printed logos, copied reference composition
